findings.issue: Source ‘crouched backwards’ became candidate ‘crouched down’, losing the backward recoil; and ‘the spear of Pelian ash went clean through’ became ‘the Pelian ash shaft went clean through’, which implies only the shaft pierced the shield.
findings.fix: Next it was Achilles’s turn to throw. His spear struck the round shield of Aeneas right at the rim, where the bronze was thinnest, and the spear of Pelian ash went clean through. The shield rang under the blow. Aeneas was afraid. He crouched backward and held the shield out away from his body. The spear flew over his back and stuck quivering in the ground, after piercing both rings of the shield that sheltered him. Aeneas had avoided it, but he stood rooted, blinded by fear and grief, because the weapon had come so close. Then Achilles sprang at him in fury, with a deadly cry and his sharp sword drawn. Aeneas picked up a great stone, so huge that two men of today could not have lifted it, though Aeneas swung it easily by himself.

findings.issue: Butler’s typo ‘You be low’ is read sensibly as ‘You lie low’ in the candidate; no change needed.
